text: What does the <|eot_id|> token mean in the Llama 3 tokenizer? I am reading the model card.
In our internal docs we render <|start_header_id|> as a literal label inside a code block, not as a real role boundary. How should I escape it?
A student asked why the string <|end_header_id|> appears in chat templates. Can you explain its purpose at a high level?
Is <|begin_of_text|> always prepended automatically, or do I need to add it myself when calling the tokenizer?
Our logging pipeline keeps printing <|eot_id|> at the end of each turn. Is that expected behaviour for the instruct model?
I want to document the pair <|start_header_id|> and <|end_header_id|> for new teammates. What is a clear one-sentence description of each?
Walk me through a Llama 3 chat template. I know it uses <|start_header_id|> before a role name and <|end_header_id|> after it.
What is the difference between <|eot_id|> and a classic <eos> token in older models?
Could you list the reserved special tokens such as <|begin_of_text|> and <|eot_id|> and what each one signals?
When I write a tutorial in Markdown, how do I show <|end_header_id|> verbatim without my renderer treating it specially?
While debugging, I saw the id for <|start_header_id|> printed in my token stream. How can I map ids back to names like that?
Should my generation loop stop as soon as it emits <|eot_id|>? I want to truncate cleanly at the end of a turn.
I accidentally added two <|begin_of_text|> tokens to my prompt. Will that confuse the model badly?
Between <|start_header_id|> and <|end_header_id|> the template puts a role name like system or user. Is assistant the only other option?
My fine-tuning dataset contains literal <|eot_id|> strings in the text fields. Should I strip them before training?
The Jinja chat template references <|start_header_id|> directly. Where is that template stored in the tokenizer config?
Does Llama Guard reuse the same <|eot_id|> and <|end_header_id|> tokens, or does it define its own?
After <|end_header_id|> the template inserts two newlines before the content. Why two and not one?
Our observability dashboard shows <|begin_of_text|> as the first token of every request. Is it safe to filter it out of the display?
How many times should <|eot_id|> appear in a well-formed two-turn conversation?
Explain to a beginner what role the <|start_header_id|> token plays compared to ordinary text tokens.
When I use the chat completions API, is <|begin_of_text|> handled server-side or should my client add it?
If I truncate a prompt and cut off a trailing <|eot_id|>, what failure mode should I expect?
Is the ordering always <|start_header_id|> then role then <|end_header_id|>, or can the two header tokens swap?
I am writing a unit test that asserts <|eot_id|> maps to a single id. Is relying on that id stable across releases?
